KhatmGuide.title: How to Organize a Group Quran Khatm
KhatmGuide.intro: A practical method for creating one shared circle, inviting readers, letting participants claim available Juz, and following the group's progress through completion.
KhatmGuide.heroLedgerFooter: Available, claimed, and read portions stay visible to the whole group.
KhatmGuide.quickAnswer: Set a clear deadline, create a link-only or public QuranCircle circle, and share its link. Readers choose an available Juz by name—no participant account required—then mark it read when finished. The same live view shows everyone what remains.
KhatmGuide.terminologyTitle: Khatm, Khatam, Khatma, Khatmah, and Hatim
KhatmGuide.terminologyText: These spellings commonly refer to completing the Quran. English speakers may write Khatm, Khatam, Khatma, Khatmah, or Khitmah; Turkish speakers commonly use Hatim. QuranCircle uses “Khatm” for the shared completion and “Juz” for each of the Quran's 30 portions.
KhatmGuide.stepsTitle: Organize the Khatm in six clear steps
KhatmGuide.stepsDescription: The tool matters, but good coordination starts with a simple agreement about the goal, timing, and responsibilities.

steps.oneText: State who the Khatm is for and when recitation should be complete. Use an exact date and time, including the time zone when readers are in different countries.
steps.twoText: Use a link-only circle for families, friends, classes, and private masjid groups. Choose public only when you want anyone browsing QuranCircle to discover and join.
steps.threeText: Give the circle a recognizable name, add a short description, and set the target date. QuranCircle prepares all 30 Juz as available portions in one live view.
steps.fourText: Put the purpose, deadline, and claim link in one short message. Ask each reader to use the same link so the live tracker remains the source of truth.
steps.fiveText: Each reader opens the link, enters their name, and claims any available Juz. The shared state prevents two people from accidentally taking the same portion.
steps.sixText: Readers mark their Juz as read when finished. Check what remains before the deadline, send a warm reminder if needed, and thank the group when all 30 are complete.

faq.oneQuestion: What is a group Quran Khatm?
faq.oneAnswer: A group Quran Khatm is a collective completion of the Quran. Readers contribute by claiming one or more of its 30 Juz, and the group completes the full recitation together.
faq.twoQuestion: How does QuranCircle coordinate all 30 Juz?
faq.twoAnswer: The organizer shares one circle link. Each reader claims an available Juz, which prevents duplicate claims, and the same view updates as portions are claimed and read.
faq.threeQuestion: Do participants need a QuranCircle account?
faq.threeAnswer: No. Participants can open the shared link and claim a Juz by name without creating an account. Organizers sign in so they can manage their circles.
faq.fourQuestion: Can the same person claim more than one Juz?
faq.fourAnswer: Yes. A reader can claim multiple available Juz, which is useful for small groups or when a deadline is approaching.
faq.fiveQuestion: Should a family Khatm be public?
faq.fiveAnswer: Usually no. A link-only circle is the better default for a family or private group because it stays off the public Browse page while remaining easy to share.
faq.sixQuestion: Do Khatm, Khatam, Khatma, and Hatim mean the same thing?
faq.sixAnswer: They are common transliterations used for completing the Quran, although spelling varies by language and community. QuranCircle uses Khatm in English and Hatim in Turkish.

faq.title: Questions about group Khatms on WhatsApp

item1.question: Can WhatsApp itself track a group Quran Khatm?
item1.answer: WhatsApp can carry invitations and reminders, but its message history is not a reliable live tracker. A shared QuranCircle link gives every participant the current list of available, claimed, and read Juz.

item2.question: Do participants need to leave the WhatsApp group?
item2.answer: No. The WhatsApp group remains useful for conversation and encouragement. Participants only open the shared circle link when they need to claim, check, unclaim, or mark a Juz read.

item3.question: Do participants need a QuranCircle account?
item3.answer: No. Readers can claim an available Juz by name without creating an account. The organizer signs in to create and manage the circle.

item4.question: What happens if someone cannot finish their Juz?
item4.answer: Ask them to unclaim the portion from the same shared link as early as possible. It becomes available again, so another reader can take it without the organizer rebuilding the list.

faq.title: Common questions about Ramadan group Khatms

item1.question: Do I need 30 people for a Ramadan group Khatm?
item1.answer: No. The Quran has 30 Juz, but a group Khatm does not require 30 readers. One participant can claim more than one available Juz, so the same shared circle works for a small family or a larger community.

item2.question: Should I assign every reader a Juz in advance?
item2.answer: You can, but self-claiming is usually easier to maintain. Readers choose an available Juz based on their capacity, and the live circle prevents two people from accidentally taking the same portion.

item3.question: Should a Ramadan family Khatm be public?
item3.answer: Usually not. A link-only QuranCircle circle stays off the public Browse page while remaining easy to send to family and friends. Choose public only when anyone should be able to discover and join.

item4.question: What if a reader falls behind?
item4.answer: Encourage the reader to unclaim the Juz early if they cannot finish. The portion becomes available again in the same live circle, allowing someone else to take it before the deadline.

item5.question: Can the group complete more than one Khatm?
item5.answer: Yes. A QuranCircle event can continue into additional Khatm cycles, allowing an ongoing group to keep the same shared circle rather than starting its coordination from scratch.
